sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: L5: tagged receptor used directly in functional assays (wild-type FP receptor with N-terminal HA SP + Flag-tag), implying receptor is functional. L6: surface expression level quantified by HiBiT luminescence. L4: stable HEK293/EBNA cell lines confirmed surface expression by immunofluorescence/ELISA.
sites.rationale: The N-terminus of PTGFR is extracellular (EC1: residues 1–29, 29 residues from TM1 boundary at residue 30), making it the only extracellular terminus available for a prepend tag on this GPCR. Two independent papers (PMC2440084, PMC10709307) report full-length FP receptor constructs with an exogenous signal peptide followed by a Flag (or HA+Flag+HiBiT) tag at the N-terminus that traffic to the plasma membrane and support functional characterization. Critically, L2 documents that the tag alone without an exogenous SP fails to reach the surface, so any ALFA-tag application must include a heterologous signal peptide preceding the tag. Python verification confirms residue 1 = M and the 29-residue EC1 span provides ample room for a 15–23 aa insert. Two independent studies (PMC2440084 and PMC10709307) expressed full-length human FP receptor with an exogenous signal peptide (prolactin SP or HA SP) followed by a Flag epitope tag at the N-terminus in HEK293 cells. L5 explicitly states the tagged receptor was used for functional assays; L6 quantified surface expression via HiBiT. L3 provides the exact construct sequence confirming the tag is placed immediately after signal peptide cleavage, before FP residue 1. No residue number is stated; the N-terminus (EC1: 1–29) is the sole extracellular terminus of this GPCR, so insert_after_residue=0 is topology-derived.

sources.claim: For functional assays, we used the wild-type human FP receptor and human EP3 receptor (isoform A) with an N-terminal HA signal peptide and Flag-tag.

literature_notes: All six N-terminal tag ledger lines (L1–L6) converge on the same junction (insert_after_residue=0), so they constitute one site, not multiple. L2 is an important caveat: the tag alone at the N-terminus does not support surface localization in the absence of an exogenous signal peptide; the validated construct requires [heterologous SP][tag][FP M1…]. L7 (LgBiT at C-terminus) and L8/L9 (bRIL in ICL3) are intracellular insertions and are recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports any extracellular loop (ECL1/ECL2/ECL3/ECL4) insertion for PTGFR.

literature_other_positions.note: LgBiT inserted at the C-terminus of full-length human FP receptor by homologous recombination; the C-terminus falls in IC4 (residues 308–359), which is intracellular.
bRIL (apocytochrome b562RIL) inserted between residues 232–239 of ICL3 (IC3: 226–250) gave the highest purification yield (0.542 mg/L); ICL3 is intracellular, not a surface-tag site.
bRIL insertions tested across ICL3 residues 231–239 (IC3: 226–250); all positions are intracellular.
